record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can one devise a reasonable numerical-relativity evolution scheme that preserves the Einstein constraint equations and can serve as a step toward proving convergence of a numerical scheme to a long-time solution of the Einstein equations?

evidence.quote: Devise a reasonable scheme which can be shown to preserve the constraints (cf. [DS]). This may also be thought of as a step towards showing convergence of some numerical scheme to a (long time) solution of the Einstein equations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein vacuum equations Ric(g) = 0 for a Lorentzian metric g on a 4-manifold, formulated as a Cauchy problem with initial data (Σ, h, K) on a spacelike hypersurface Σ, where h is a Riemannian metric and K a symmetric 2-tensor satisfying the Einstein constraint equations

  R(h) + (tr_h K)^2 − |K|_h^2 = 0,   div_h K − d(tr_h K) = 0.

Under any 3+1 decomposition, the evolution equations propagate the constraints analytically: if the constraints hold on the initial slice, they hold on every later slice of the maximal globally hyperbolic development. In a numerical discretization, however, this exact propagation generally fails, and constraint violations may grow and destroy convergence.

Problem. Design a numerical evolution scheme for the Einstein equations (in some well-posed 3+1 formulation, with appropriate gauge and boundary conditions) such that:

(a) The discrete solution exactly (or in a controlled, provably bounded sense) satisfies discrete analogues of the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints at every time step, for arbitrary admissible discrete initial data satisfying the discrete constraints;

(b) The scheme admits a rigorous proof of convergence, as the discretization parameters tend to zero, to a (long-time) smooth solution of the Einstein equations, at least within some nontrivial regime of initial data (e.g., a neighborhood of Minkowski space or another stable background).

Either exhibit such a scheme together with proofs of constraint preservation and long-time convergence, or prove that no such scheme exists under stated reasonable hypotheses.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of devising a numerical-relativity scheme that exactly preserves the Einstein constraints and admits a rigorous long-time convergence proof remains open. Recent work (e.g., structure-preserving Hodge–Dirac and divdiv-complex discretizations of the linearized Einstein equations, and adjusted BSSN systems) has produced partial results: well-posedness and error estimates in linearized or constrained formulations, and empirical control of constraint violations. However, full constraint preservation (in particular of the Hamiltonian constraint) together with rigorous convergence to long-time solutions of the nonlinear Einstein equations has not been achieved.

status_evidence.title: Hodge-Dirac wave systems and structure-preserving discretizations of the linearized Einstein equations
status_evidence.snippet: Discretization scheme established with well-posedness and error estimates for the time-dependent linearized problem; constraints preserved via complex structure.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress on structure-preserving discretizations is limited to the linearized setting.

status_evidence.title: Numerical experiments of adjusted BSSN systems for controlling constraint violations
status_evidence.snippet: Adjusted BSSN systems are studied numerically to control, not eliminate, constraint violations.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art evolution schemes only control constraint growth empirically.

status_evidence.title: New and old problems in Numerical Relativity
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous understanding of convergence properties remains unresolved in numerical relativity.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous long-time convergence of numerical schemes for Einstein's equations is still open.
